name: Integration Testing Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for integration testing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for integration testing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious integration testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Prefer the simplest integration testing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. When integration testing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
4. Keep integration testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Keep integration testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Check that integration testing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
7. Before starting integration testing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to integration testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. When multiple integration testing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
10. When integration testing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
11. State assumptions about integration testing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
12. Surface known limitations of a chosen integration testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of integration testing correctness.
- Do not apply generic integration testing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting integration testing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new integration testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for integration testing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
